display.purpose: Cover wordmark only; colophon repeats it at clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem).

headline.purpose: Page titles: catalogue, game, jams, publish.

section.purpose: Home section heads; track band names run at width 50%.

title.purpose: Entry titles; lead/wide entries step up, row entries step down.

numeral.purpose: Times, entry numbers, prices, counts, steps, scores. Always tabular.

code.purpose: Platform legend letters (N W M L A) and thumb-index tab names.

body-lead.purpose: Section intros, band blurbs, long-form game description (1.65 line height in prose).

label.purpose: Field labels, fieldset legends, card state lines, colophon headings. Sentence case.

shadows.name: lift

shadows.name: input-halo
shadows.purpose: Focused text inputs and textareas, with background shifting to #f5f7f9.

shadows.name: tab-pull-rail
shadows.purpose: Active thumb-index tab on the desktop rail.

shadows.name: tab-pull-strip
shadows.purpose: Active thumb-index tab on the mobile strip.

shadows.name: live-glow
shadows.purpose: The jam schedule's 'agora' line. Live state only.

shadows.purpose: The 9px lime live dot. Live state only.

strokes.name: rule
strokes.purpose: Programme rule: masthead, page heads, bands, results bar, step and list openers; also every control and container border.

strokes.name: double-rule
strokes.purpose: Under every section head and list title.

strokes.name: hair
strokes.purpose: Between rows in ruled lists, fieldsets and pitch rows.

strokes.name: foot-rule

strokes.name: slot-dash

narrative.overview:
openitch is printed, not rendered. Every page is a spread from a festival programme book: cool grey newsprint, blue-black ink, and spot colours laid down as solid fields. A track does not wear its colour as a badge; it owns a whole band of the page, a page head, a game stage, a card. Ink draws the structure with 2px programme rules and a 6px double rule that opens each section. Everything else sits flat on the paper.

The voice is condensed and loud at the top and plain and readable below. Anybody, pulled narrow, carries the wordmark, section titles, entry titles and every number the programme prints: entry numbers (Nº 0142), times, prices, counts, scores. Schibsted Grotesk carries reading text and every control. Density is a printed schedule's: ruled rows, tabular figures, legend codes for platforms (N W M L A), and entries billed at different sizes rather than repeated as equal tiles.

The page has one wayfinding device of its own, the thumb index: coloured tabs on the page edge, one per track, like the cut tabs of a printed guide. Motion is small and physical (a tab slides out, a card lifts a few pixels, a field recolours). Light is kept for one meaning only: something is live right now.
keyCharacteristics: Cool newsprint paper (never warm cream) with blue-black ink; the page is flat.
Five spot colours, one per track, used as full fields with ink on top (paper on ultramarine only).
Anybody at condensed widths for display and numerals; Schibsted Grotesk for text and UI.
2px ink programme rules for structure, 1px faint hairlines between rows, 6px double rules under section heads.
Pill controls and pill-ended bars with 2px ink borders; cards and sheets with 12–16px corners and 2px ink borders.
Thumb-index tabs, entry numbers and platform legend codes as the recurring programme furniture.
Glow appears only on live state.

rules.name: The Full Field Rule
rules.body: A track colour is laid down as a field: a band, a page head, a game stage, a jam card, a preview sheet, the hover fill of a schedule row. The only small use is the 12–14px ink-bordered swatch that keys a track name in a legend or chip.

rules.name: The Ink On Spot Rule
rules.body: Text on lime, tangerine, magenta and teal is ink; text on ultramarine and on ink is paper. No other text colour sits on a spot field.

rules.name: The Lime Means Go Rule
rules.body: Off its own track, lime marks the action on a field, a confirmation or selection, or something live. It is never decoration.

rules.name: The Narrow Voice Rule
rules.body: Anybody is always condensed: 50–58% for display and page heads, 60–70% for titles and times, 70–80% for codes, prices and entry numbers. It never runs at its default width.

rules.name: The Printed Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number the programme prints (entry number, time, price, count, step, score) is set in Anybody with tabular figures. Schibsted Grotesk never carries a headline number.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels, legends and buttons are sentence case Schibsted Grotesk. Nothing in the system is set in uppercase or letter-spaced caps.

rules.name: The Billing Rule
rules.body: Entries vary in scale by billing (lead, wide, card, row). Never fill a surface with a row of equal cards.

rules.name: The Ruled List Rule
rules.body: A list of entries or events is a ruled programme list with a numeral column, not a stack of boxes.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow is a response to hover, never a resting state.

rules.name: The Glow Means Live Rule
rules.body: Glow and pulse belong only to something happening now: the schedule's "agora" line, a live dot. Nothing else glows.

dos: Do lay a track's colour down as a whole field (band, page head, stage, card, sheet) and pass it to components as `--c` and `--on`.
Do set ink on lime, tangerine, magenta and teal, and paper on ultramarine and ink.
Do draw structure with ink: 2px solid rules for edges, a 6px double rule under section heads, 1px hairlines at 28% ink between rows.
Do give controls and containers a 2px ink border; use full pills (999px) for buttons, toggles, tags and bars, and 10–16px corners for fields, cards and sheets.
Do set every printed number (Nº entry number, time, price, count, step) in condensed Anybody with tabular figures.
Do show all five platform legend codes (N W M L A) and fade the absent ones to 22%.
Do bill entries at different sizes (lead, wide, card, row) and print lists as ruled rows with a numeral column.

Do keep motion short and physical on the shared ease-out curve (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)): 160–180ms for controls, 220–260ms for tabs and underlines, 320ms for entry lift, 420ms for a field recolour; honour reduced motion.
donts: Don't use a track colour as a small sticker, badge or text accent on paper; the only small form is the ink-bordered legend swatch.
Don't set Anybody at its default width or use it for reading text or controls.
Don't glow, pulse or neon-light anything that is not live right now.
Don't give surfaces a resting shadow; lift only on hover.
Don't warm the paper toward cream or darken the page into a gamer-store black; the page is cool newsprint and ink.
Don't set labels or buttons in uppercase or letter-spaced caps.
Don't use lime off its own track for anything except an action on a field, a confirmation or selection, or live state.
